primary_prior_art.title: On the Complexity of Robust Markov Decision Processes and Bisimulation Metrics

finding: Action-conditioned recursive MDP bisimulation-metric computation is existing prior art with an official pinned implementation. The implementation is an exact known-model metric baseline, not a finite-sample full-consequence partition estimator and not a solution for Q or d.
counterexamples: A standard reward-transition bisimulation metric can assign distance zero while a preregistered independent physical consequence differs.
An exact solver for a supplied point MDP cannot identify which of two finite-sample-compatible point MDPs generated the data.
Thresholding a pseudometric does not automatically yield a transitive approximate partition.
Semantic reward or target-derived labels leak the ontology into the metric.

baseline_update.selected: Suilen-Perez exact known-model action-conditioned metric baseline
baseline_update.remaining: finite-sample leakage-free full-consequence controlled partition estimator with coverage abstention and a global approximate-partition contract
